author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if happiness could be taught, practiced, and measured like any other academic skill? Dr. Ashleigh Maxcey introduces a radical pedagogical approach that assigns and grades happiness-building activities. In this provocative talk, she reveals how mandatory joy assignments offer the best chance at happiness, from the classroom to the boardroom, by treating it as the foundation for everything else.   

Dr. Ashleigh Maxcey is a Research Assistant Professor and Senior Lecturer at Vanderbilt University's Department of Psychology and a pioneering educator in the science of happiness. By creating a groundbreaking positive psychology course that grades students on engagement with intentional joy-building activities, she challenges traditional academic paradigms and demonstrates how happiness can be systematically learned and practiced. title: How to start putting your happiness first | Ashleigh Maxcey | TEDxNashville

author: TEDx Talks
description: On the night she lost her mother, a daughter sang “Que sera, sera” at the bedside of a woman that had already taken away once before. In this deeply personal talk, Marianne shares the invisible labor, burnout, love, and small sensory rituals that helped her reach her mother through the fog of dementia, and explains why she now fights publicly against stigma and for a radically better, more humane system for people living with dementia and their families. Marianne Mørck Danielsen is a dynamic communicator, strategist, and organizational developer with over two decades of experience helping people and organizations grow through culture, communication, and leadership. Based in Trondheim, Norway, she is also a passionate advocate for dementia awareness, drawing from her deeply personal journey as a caregiver to her mother. As an independent consultant, author, and host of the podcast Ikke lett å glemme, Marianne brings together professional insight and human storytelling to inspire change
title: How dementia redefines love, identity, and presence | Marianne Mørck Danielsen | TEDxBodø

author: TEDx Talks
description:
María Nicole nos invita a reflexionar sobre el conflicto humano entre el deseo de experimentar todas las posibilidades de la vida y la necesidad inevitable de tomar decisiones que cierran caminos. Su charla explora cómo este impulso de vivir múltiples vidas puede generar ansiedad en la sociedad actual, apoyándose en conceptos psicológicos como el FOMO y la paradoja de la elección de Barry Schwartz, así como en la filosofía existencialista de Sartre. 

Asimismo, muestra que elegir no es perder, sino comprometerse conscientemente con la vida que queremos construir. Su mensaje final busca empoderar a la audiencia, recordándonos que la clave no está en vivirlo todo, sino en vivir con intención y coherencia, tomando decisiones que reflejen nuestras prioridades y valores más auténticos.  Durante mi etapa escolar he desarrollado un gran interés por las humanidades, la tecnología y la comunicación, lo que me ha llevado a participar como Secretaria Académica del Modelo de Naciones Unidas IX de
title: La paradoja de querer vivirlo todo | Maria Nicole Rodriguez Martinez | TEDxLCB Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: “I hope an asteroid wipes us all out so no one mourns me”: a seven‑year‑old’s words spark a deeper question—what if the real “end of the world” isn’t planetary doom, but a dystopia where culture stops evolving amid climate displacement?  Drawing from community dance in rubbish dumps, refugee camps, and his own shift from ballet to *transilient* arts activism, Nicholas argues that participatory arts education can teach us Sumud (steadfastness) to regenerate new cultures, democracies, and futures as up to 1 billion people face forced migration by 2050. Nicholas Rowe is UNESCO Chair of Dance and Social Inclusion and bridges the worlds of dance, community, and politics through research, teaching, and creative practice. A graduate of the Australian Ballet School with a PhD from the London Contemporary Dance School, Nicholas has performed and choreographed internationally with leading companies including The Finnish National Ballet, Australian Ballet, and Royal New Zealand Ballet. His work
title: Can dancing prepare democracy for dystopia? | Nicholas Rowe | TEDxBodø

author: TEDx Talks
description: Terrified of physics and sure she was “always wrong,” Hannah nearly gave up—until she realized her mistakes were not proof of failure but the raw material of learning itself. In a talk full of magnets, feathers, bowling balls, buggy code, and even tough cookies, she shows how treating errors as "seeds" or “bugs” to investigate can rebuild confidence, deepen understanding, and turn fear of failure into curiosity and creativity in any field. Hannah C. Sabo holds a Ph.D. in Science Education from the University of Maryland (2021), with a B.S. in Physics and Applied Mathematics from Seattle Pacific University. She has taught physics at both the University of Maryland and Seattle Pacific, focusing on inquiry-based instruction for future educators. Her research explores students’ conceptual understanding in physics and how STEM faculty integrate and assess computation in their teaching. Hannah has published in Physical Review Physics Education Research and contributes to research on computa
title: How to stop fearing mistakes and start celebrating them | Hannah Sabo | TEDxBodø

description: ¿Qué pasaría si la verdadera innovación no viniera de la tecnología ni de la IA, sino del tiempo que nos devuelve? Esta charla revela cómo el liberar a las personas de sus rutinas y tareas repetitivas puede desatar creatividad, nuevas ideas y hasta modelos de negocio inesperados. La IA no sustituye al humano: lo expande. Francisco es un líder en innovación tecnológica y transformación empresarial con más de 35 años impulsando el desarrollo de soluciones que conectan estrategia, tecnología y creatividad humana. Ha dedicado su carrera a construir capacidades que permitan a las organizaciones evolucionar, modernizar sus operaciones y adoptar tecnologías emergentes de forma práctica y responsable. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Julián nos invita a reflexionar sobre cómo las grandes transformaciones del mundo nacen muchas veces de ideas modestas, cuyo valor no reside en los recursos disponibles, sino en la determinación y la creatividad de quienes las ponen en acción. A través de ejemplos emblemáticos como la creación de Apple, los primeros vuelos de la aviación y los descubrimientos de Einstein y Mendel, nos muestra que toda innovación comienza con una chispa de curiosidad y perseverancia. 

Su charla destaca cómo la tecnología, la ciencia y la ingeniería han sido motores del progreso humano y cómo la innovación frugal —aquella que surge con pocos recursos— puede tener un impacto global. Julián nos recuerda que incluso la idea más pequeña, cuando se impulsa con convicción, tiene el poder de redefinir lo conocido y transformar la sociedad A nivel escolar me he caracterizado por ser una persona responsable, comprometida y con enfoque constante hacia la excelencia. title: El poder oculto de una idea pequeña | Julián Alejandro Cely Mongui | TEDxLCB Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: VOLT Co-Founder Damian Boeselager reflects on how political disengagement weakens democracy and why active citizenship is more important than ever. Drawing on his own path into European politics, he shows that meaningful change does not start with power or titles, but with individuals who choose to get involved. His talk is a call to move beyond apathy and recognize that a functioning society depends on the participation of all of us. Damian Boeselager is a co-founder of Volt Europa, a pan-European political movement advocating for a more democratic, transparent, and united European Union. Since 2019, he has served as a Member of the European Parliament, where he works on economic governance, institutional reform, and democratic resilience. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Politics and Me – Why Society Needs All of Us | Damian Boeselager | TEDxHHU

description:
We either being student or a professional, often wait for confidence, clarity or perfect conditions before taking our first step or any decision but life rarely gives us that certainty. I want to focus on that the readiness must come before action and explores how growth begins the moment we choose courage over fear.

 Dr. Kainat Gohar is a Homoeopathic healthcare professional, entrepreneur and a trainer with over six years of experience spanning medicine, innovation and social impact. She is the Founder and CEO of OrganiCure, CEO of Eilaajverse and holds the role of leadership and entrepreneurship trainer at Pakistan Blockchain Institute where she works on future focused healthcare, emerging technologies and leadership development.

Alongside her clinical expertise in Homeopathy, Homoeopathic dermatology, aesthetics, and hair transplant procedures, she is also a public speaker, social worker, and community leader actively involved in education, innovation, and humanitarian initiative
title: The Power of Starting Before You're Ready | Kainat Gohar | TEDxNamalUniversity

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk challenges the culture of only sharing polished success and “after the struggle” stories. It argues that true courage lies in showing our real, mid-struggle moments with honesty. By doing so, we give others permission to feel without shame and the comfort of knowing they are not alone. The message shifts from individual self-help to collective empathy and stronger community. Dua is a dedicated first-year BSCS student at Namal University from Faisalabad, committed to the genuine and often challenging process of learning. She is currently focused on building a strong foundation in Computer Science and actively engaging with her coursework. Dua believes that the most meaningful gift one can offer others is the radical generosity of sharing authentic, mid-struggle moments. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Radical Generosity of Showing Your Bad Day | Dua . | TEDxNamalUniversity
